rewritten_query:
WITH params AS (
    SELECT d_month_seq
    FROM date_dim
    WHERE d_date = DATE '2001-03-21'
),
ss_items AS (
    SELECT i.i_item_id AS item_id,
           c.c_birth_year AS birth_year,
           SUM(ss.ss_ext_sales_price) AS ss_item_rev
    FROM store_sales ss
    JOIN item i ON ss.ss_item_sk = i.i_item_sk
    JOIN date_dim d ON ss.ss_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
    JOIN customer c ON ss.ss_customer_sk = c.c_customer_sk
    JOIN params p ON d.d_month_seq = p.d_month_seq
    WHERE ss.ss_list_price BETWEEN 265 AND 294
      AND i.i_manager_id BETWEEN 37 AND 66
      AND c.c_birth_year BETWEEN 1936 AND 1942
    GROUP BY i.i_item_id, c.c_birth_year
),
cs_items AS (
    SELECT i.i_item_id AS item_id,
           c.c_birth_year AS birth_year,
           SUM(cs.cs_ext_sales_price) AS cs_item_rev
    FROM catalog_sales cs
    JOIN item i ON cs.cs_item_sk = i.i_item_sk
    JOIN date_dim d ON cs.cs_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
    JOIN customer c ON cs.cs_bill_customer_sk = c.c_customer_sk
    JOIN params p ON d.d_month_seq = p.d_month_seq
    WHERE cs.cs_list_price BETWEEN 265 AND 294
      AND i.i_manager_id BETWEEN 37 AND 66
      AND c.c_birth_year BETWEEN 1936 AND 1942
    GROUP BY i.i_item_id, c.c_birth_year
),
ws_items AS (
    SELECT i.i_item_id AS item_id,
           c.c_birth_year AS birth_year,
           SUM(ws.ws_ext_sales_price) AS ws_item_rev
    FROM web_sales ws
    JOIN item i ON ws.ws_item_sk = i.i_item_sk
    JOIN date_dim d ON ws.ws_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
    JOIN customer c ON ws.ws_bill_customer_sk = c.c_customer_sk
    JOIN params p ON d.d_month_seq = p.d_month_seq
    WHERE ws.ws_list_price BETWEEN 265 AND 294
      AND i.i_manager_id BETWEEN 37 AND 66
      AND c.c_birth_year BETWEEN 1936 AND 1942
    GROUP BY i.i_item_id, c.c_birth_year
)
SELECT ssi.item_id,
       ssi.birth_year,
       ssi.ss_item_rev,
       ssi.ss_item_rev / ((ssi.ss_item_rev + csi.cs_item_rev + wsi.ws_item_rev) / 3.0) * 100 AS ss_dev,
       csi.cs_item_rev,
       csi.cs_item_rev / ((ssi.ss_item_rev + csi.cs_item_rev + wsi.ws_item_rev) / 3.0) * 100 AS cs_dev,
       wsi.ws_item_rev,
       wsi.ws_item_rev / ((ssi.ss_item_rev + csi.cs_item_rev + wsi.ws_item_rev) / 3.0) * 100 AS ws_dev,
       (ssi.ss_item_rev + csi.cs_item_rev + wsi.ws_item_rev) / 3.0 AS average
FROM ss_items ssi
JOIN cs_items csi
  ON ssi.item_id = csi.item_id
 AND ssi.birth_year = csi.birth_year
JOIN ws_items wsi
  ON ssi.item_id = wsi.item_id
 AND ssi.birth_year = wsi.birth_year
WHERE ssi.ss_item_rev BETWEEN 0.9 * csi.cs_item_rev AND 1.1 * csi.cs_item_rev
  AND ssi.ss_item_rev BETWEEN 0.9 * wsi.ws_item_rev AND 1.1 * wsi.ws_item_rev
  AND csi.cs_item_rev BETWEEN 0.9 * ssi.ss_item_rev AND 1.1 * ssi.ss_item_rev
  AND csi.cs_item_rev BETWEEN 0.9 * wsi.ws_item_rev AND 1.1 * wsi.ws_item_rev
  AND wsi.ws_item_rev BETWEEN 0.9 * ssi.ss_item_rev AND 1.1 * ssi.ss_item_rev
  AND wsi.ws_item_rev BETWEEN 0.9 * csi.cs_item_rev AND 1.1 * csi.cs_item_rev
ORDER BY ssi.item_id, ssi.birth_year, ssi.ss_item_rev
LIMIT 100;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Replaced the nested `d_date IN (SELECT d_date FROM date_dim WHERE d_month_seq = (SELECT ...))` semi-join with a direct `d_month_seq` equality join. Since d_date is unique in date_dim, this is semantically equivalent and allows the planner to use the d_month_seq index to fetch only ~30 dates instead of scanning/joining date_dim via a hash semi-join in each CTE.

Introduced a `params` CTE that computes the target d_month_seq once (referenced 3 times, so it is materialized/computed once) instead of repeating the scalar subquery against date_dim in all three channel CTEs.
Converted implicit comma joins into explicit ANSI JOINs with aliases, improving readability and making the join tree unambiguous; join keys (item_sk, date_sk, customer_sk) are preserved exactly.

Used 3.0 in division to keep numeric semantics explicit; all other constants (list price range, manager id range, birth year range, 0.9/1.1 revenue ratios, LIMIT 100) are preserved as-is since they are already literals the optimizer can fold.
